title: Enterprise onboarding + escalation + integration + QBR playbook
author: Maya Singh
body:
Overview

This document consolidates the standard operating playbook for enterprise onboarding at Redwood Inference: step-by-step onboarding checklist, integration guide (API + Dedicated + webhooks), escalation playbook for customer-impacting incidents, known issues and pragmatic workarounds, and a QBR/health-check template for ongoing account reviews. It is written for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and SRE owners.

Scope

- Applies to all enterprise customers (Dedicated, Private, and hosted API with enterprise agreement).
- Covers technical integration, operational readiness, escalation paths, and quarterly business reviews (QBRs).

Prerequisites (before technical onboarding)

1. Signed contract with identified points of contact (primary CSM, technical lead, security contact).
2. Billing and invoicing contacts recorded in Salesforce.
3. Access request for customer console + support portal provisioned.

Onboarding checklist (high level)

1. Kickoff (Week 0)
   - Introductions: CSM, SE, customer technical lead, and if applicable, account executive (AE).
   - Share onboarding doc, Slack channel (#cs-<customer-short>), and support expectations.

2. Requirements & Network (Week 0-1)
   - Confirm model(s) to serve and expected traffic profile (RPS, average sequence length, burst characteristics).
   - For Dedicated/Private: collect VPC/subnet/netflow and KMS/HSM integration details; set IP allowlists.
   - Security review: sign off on data handling, retention, and logging requirements.

3. Integration & Test Plan (Week 1-3)
   - Provide SE integration guide and sample code; run smoke tests; confirm auth and model access.
   - Validate end-to-end latency and throughput against target SLOs.
   - Create a synthetic workload (QA prompts) for regression monitoring.

4. Operational Readiness (Week 2-4)
   - Configure alerting thresholds (error rate > 0.5%, p95 latency > target, 429 rate > baseline).
   - Share runbook access and incident contacts.
   - Onboard customer to Redwood Console dashboards and cost breakdowns.

5. Go-live and Hypercare (Week 4-6)
   - Coordinate canary rollout (10-20% traffic), monitor error/latency, and complete full rollout once stable.
   - Run two-week hypercare with daily syncs, then weekly until QBR cadence starts.

Integration guide (technical)

Auth and endpoints
- Hosted API: https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1
- Dedicated: base URL provided per-customer (e.g., https://dedicated-<customer>.redwood.internal)
- Authentication: standard Bearer token (api_key). For Private deployments, use customer-provided KMS keys for secrets.
- Sample curl: 
  curl -X POST \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","input":"Summarize the following..."}' \
    https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate

Model pinning and rollouts
- Use the model_version param to pin a model; use rollout policies to canary (percent) traffic.
- For Dedicated customers, recommend creating a staging route mirrored to a production route for safe rollouts.

Webhooks and observability
- Customers can register webhooks for deployment and health events: /v1/webhooks/register.
- Direct customers to Redwood Console > Customers > <ID> > Routes for per-route latency, token usage, and trace links.

Common integration checks (SE checklist)
- Confirm token scopes and expiry.
- Verify sample prompts produce expected output shape and that function/tool-calling works.
- Validate cache headers and streaming behavior if used.

Escalation playbook (customer-impacting incidents)

Goals: shortest possible time-to-restoration while communicating clearly to the customer.

Severity definitions
- Sev-1 (Critical): Production outage impacting >50% of customer traffic or data loss. Target MTTR: < 2 hours (pager).
- Sev-2 (High): Significant degradation (latency p95 > SLO x 2 or error rate > 2%) impacting core functionality. Target MTTR: < 8 hours.
- Sev-3 (Medium): Functional but degraded (intermittent 429s, minor regressions). Target MTTR: < 3 business days.

Immediate actions (first 15 minutes)
1. Acknowledge and create incident in incident tracker (Jira/IncidentOps).
2. Notify customer channel and CSM with initial triage.
3. Triage owner (Support Eng) runs quick checks: API availability, infra capacity, recent deploys, config changes.

Escalation path
1. Support Engineer (tier 1): Slack #support-ops, PagerDuty support-oncall.
2. SE / Solutions Engineer (tier 2): Escalate if root cause unclear after 30 minutes. PagerDuty escalation to SE oncall.
3. SRE / Serving Runtime (tier 3): For infrastructure or kernel/runtime issues. Contact via PagerDuty (serving-runtime-oncall) and Slack #runtime-incident.
4. Exec/Account escalation: Notify CSM, AE, and VP Customer Success for sustained Sev-1 beyond 4 hours.

Information to collect for any escalation
- Customer ID, route ID, timestamps, sample request IDs, error messages and HTTP response codes, p95/p99 latency trends, recent deploy IDs, and relevant logs (link to Kibana/Cloudwatch/ELK).
- Attach synthetic test results and customer-provided failing prompts.

Communication cadence
- Initial update: within 15 minutes.
- Follow-ups: every 30 minutes for Sev-1, every 2 hours for Sev-2, daily for Sev-3 until resolved.

Post-incident
1. Postmortem drafted by owning team within 5 business days.
2. Customer-facing summary prepared by CSM and reviewed with Engineering.
3. Action items tracked and closed in two sprints where possible.

Known issues & workarounds (operational table)

- Issue: Tokenization mismatch with customer tokenizer
  Workaround: Pass explicit tokenizer_version param or normalize inputs client-side. For custom tokenizers, provide a pinned model variant with matching tokenizer.

- Issue: KV-cache growth causes OOM on long-lived chat sessions
  Workaround: Configure max_kv_cache_tokens=4096 or enable periodic cache eviction (SDK option: --kv-evict-interval=10m). Recommend session truncation policy for >4k tokens.

- Issue: Intermittent 429 under sudden bursts despite reserved capacity
  Workaround: Increase burst window in routing policy (burst_capacity + 30%) and enable client-side exponential backoff with jitter. Review autoscale policy.

- Issue: Slight semantic regressions after model upgrades
  Workaround: Use rollout (canary) and the evaluation harness (redwood/eval-harness) to compare regression prompts. Roll back to previous pinned model if regression fails acceptance criteria.

Log collection & triage commands (examples)
- Serving logs (for Dedicated): kubectl -n customer-<id> logs -l app=redwood-serving --since=30m | grep <route-id>
- Check Redis/KV cache memory: redis-cli INFO memory
- Fetch recent traces: curl -s "https://console.redwood.internal/api/traces?customer=<id>&since=1h"

Health checks & QBR materials

Quarterly Health/ QBR agenda (60-90 minutes)
1. Executive summary (CSM) - top metrics, uptime, and major incidents.
2. Usage trends (SE/FinOps) - RPS, tokens per month, cost trends, and forecast.
3. Quality & regressions (Applied ML) - evaluation harness results, top failed prompts, and remediation plan.
4. Performance & capacity (SRE) - p50/p95/p99 latency, cache hit rate, and autoscaling behavior.
5. Roadmap & asks (Product/Engineering) - upcoming model changes, new features, and migration plans.
6. Action items & wrap-up - owners and deadlines.

Suggested QBR metrics (presented as slides)
- Availability (monthly) - target 99.9%
- Error rate (5xx / total) - baseline and trend
- Latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99) per route/model
- Token usage and cost per 1M tokens
- Cache hit rate and effective token savings
- Top 10 latency/error-causing prompts with examples
- Active incidents since last QBR and status of action items

Templates & assets
- QBR slide template: /assets/qbr-template-redwood.pptx
- Onboarding checklist (spreadsheet): /assets/onboarding-checklist.xlsx
- Evaluation harness repo (internal): github.com/redwood/eval-harness (link in console)

Ownership & responsibilities
- CSM: coordinates onboarding schedule, QBRs, and customer communications.
- SE: leads technical integration and acceptance tests.
- Support Eng: first responder for incidents and SLA management.
- SRE / Serving Runtime: owns platform availability, runbooks, and kernel-level perf fixes.

Appendices

A. Example alert thresholds (recommended defaults)
- errors_5xx_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m -> P1 alert to #support-ops and PagerDuty.
- p95_latency > 2x target for 10m -> P1 alert to #runtime-incident.
- 429_rate > baseline + 5% for 5m -> P2 alert.

B. Quick checklist for SE smoke test
1. Auth OK (200).
2. Small generation path successful and within latency target.
3. Streaming behaves and WS connections stable for 10 concurrent clients.

C. Contact matrix
- Primary CSM: assigned per account (see Salesforce record)
- Support Slack: #support-ops
- PagerDuty services: support-oncall, serving-runtime-oncall, se-oncall

If you find gaps in this playbook, please raise a docs PR and ping @Maya in #cs-docs for triage.
